content.evidence_note: Actual source proof mechanism read in Section 3 native images and original-PDF Appendix A–C text. The long source interfaces are imported with explicit conditions and locators; no independent reproof or efficient implementation is asserted.
failure_modes: Norm clipping alone can introduce a threshold-times-confidence penalty and does not justify a small directional confidence scale.
L alone does not justify choosing s much smaller than L.
A fixed-mean estimation guarantee does not cover adaptively changing subgradient means.
Treating rejected draws or auxiliary replacement samples as free invalidates the raw-budget guarantee.
This proof method is not a full Algorithm record or an unconditional matching all-budget theorem.
content.goal_pattern: Prove high-probability online regret and composite convex optimization bounds whose leading confidence term uses directional p-moment s rather than total norm scale L.
content.key_choice: Integrate over U=Z+aN with Z supported in the virtual decision ball and independent standard Gaussian N. Use density KL plus a quadratic penalty of the density mean, not KL of mixture weights. Gaussian variables are auxiliary integration variables and consume no oracle samples.
content.key_relation: With ell_alpha=log(3/alpha), Lemma A.3 bounds (1/n)sum <b_t,z_t-u> by C_p R[(M+sqrt(V))/sqrt(n)+M ell_alpha/n+s0(ell_alpha/n)^q]. The sqrt(V/n) contribution has no leading confidence multiplier. Conditional rejection gives bias <=C_p s(L/tau)^(p-1) and V<=C_p L^p tau^(2-p), preserving directional scale up to a p-dependent constant.
proof_skeleton: Appendix A.1–A.2: split <xi,U-x>=<xi,Z-x>+a<xi,N>. The bounded direction uses its directional p-moment; Gaussian averaging uses E_N|<xi,N>|^2=||xi||^2. For chi clipping to [-1,1], establish E exp(+-[chi(eta<b+xi,U-x>)-eta<b,U-x>])<=exp(C_p[eta^p(s0 R)^p+eta^2 a^2(V+M^2)]) when 0<a<=R and eta M R<=1/16.

Appendix A.3: take a finite R/(8n)-net of the ball containing its center c and the convex family of Gaussian-mixture densities with centers in this net and common covariance a^2 I. Initialize P1=N(c,a^2 I), z_t=E_{P_t}U. After observing Y_t set Psi_t(u)=chi(eta<Y_t,u-z_t>) and minimize E_P Psi_t+KL(P||P_t)+(beta/2)||m(P)-m(P_t)||^2 over the family. Equation (21) selects a,beta,eta. Compare to N(u*,a^2 I), where u* is a nearest net point to the fixed comparator. Two product supermartingales and the dimension-free Gaussian comparison cost R^2/(2a^2) produce the online bound; the net approximation adds at most MR/(8n). No union bound over the net is used.

Appendix B.1: in the affine-hull translation space project raw subgradients and construct y=prox_{lambda h}(z), a predictable a=(z-y)/lambda with ||a||<=3G, and a nearby w in ri X with ||w-y||<=R/(8n). The transformed observation Y=Pi g(w,xi)+a has mean norm <=4G and preserves centered moments. Equation (25) gives F(y)-F*<=<EY,z-x*>+GR/(2n); no prox for an added ball constraint is assumed.

Appendix B.2: freeze w and correction throughout repeated fresh draws; accept ||Y||<=tau for tau>=64(4G+L). Centering and directional Holder control rejection bias; truncation controls total second moment. Run the online update on accepted observations and output the average corresponding feasible proximal points. At n>=C_p log(3/alpha), cap at 4n raw calls and couple to the ideal accepted process. Exhaustion is included in failure and returns a predetermined feasible proximal point; rejected values are ignored for updates but charged.

Appendix C: tau=128 max{4G+L,L(T/e)^(1/p)}, e=L^2/s^2, balances accepted second moment and bias. Use a free proximal cap, the convex primitive, or strong-convexity localization selected in advance from public parameters. For strong convexity, radii halve and delta_j=delta 2^(j-J-1); geometric budget sums absorb the stage-dependent confidence costs without an extra horizon logarithm.
content.required_inputs: Finite-dimensional Euclidean geometry, 1<p<=2, q=1-1/p. The processed online interface has predictable means ||b_t||<=M, conditional centered second moment <=V, and every conditional directional p-moment <=s0^p. Comparator u is fixed in a radius-R ball after conditioning on initial history; horizon n is fixed, M>0,V>=0,s0>0,0<alpha<1/10. Raw optimization observations instead require the two separate conditional centered p-moment bounds L^p,s^p, fresh fixed query-dependent kernels, known closed convex X and known r with exact prox_h, and a certified ball containing x*. Unknown values and reusable random functions are unavailable.
transfer_obligations: Verify both conditional moment controls at adaptive histories; static robust estimation at one fixed mean is insufficient.
Construct bounded predictable means and feasible queries using only the actual allowed prox. Do not silently assume prox for an extra localization-ball constraint.
Preserve fresh independent draws at frozen queries during rejection and charge every raw draw. Couple capped and ideal processes rather than conditioning concentration on completion.
Validate the density exponential estimate, comparator comparison and parameter choices for any changed geometry or noise model.
For a new end-to-end claim separately establish output conversion, almost-sure total budget, parameter-only selection and curvature/failure allocation.
Computational efficiency requires a new implementation analysis; the finite net and density representation may be exponentially large in dimension.
